data.content_ref: inline:The proposal self-reports the fatal guarantee break: 'the monotonicity of the sequence across stages (reopening is not monotone) breaks the fixed-point determinism guarantee.' The original grounded extension is defined as a deterministic fixed point; the problem requires preserving 'determinism of the fixed point.' SRC_002 replaces it with a staged limit where suspended nodes can be reopened in later stages via fresh edge-construction warrants. Reopening is non-monotone by construction, so the stage sequence is not guaranteed to converge to a single fixed point independent of stage ordering/timing; determinism becomes contingent on an a-priori bound and monotonicity that the proposal itself says is absent. This is a direct violation of the stated problem requirement, independent of the polynomial-cost concern.
